info.title: AWorld API - v1 Dashboard Endpoints
info.description: The Dashboard context provides APIs for administration and management functions, enabling account owners and administrators to configure and monitor their AWorld environments. These APIs are designed for use in administrative interfaces and management tools.

get.description: Returns the curated, provider-agnostic voice catalogue (with optional sample audio) proxied from the learning-path agent.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Content language to pick each voice's preview sample in.

schema.description: Content language to pick each voice's preview sample in.

post.summary: Suggest and check a competency's level descriptions
post.description: Suggests the level descriptions a competency is missing and points out written ones that describe nothing a person could see or hear, in the given language. Nothing is saved.

label.description: The competency's name in that language.

anchors.description: The level descriptions written so far. Empty ones get a suggestion; written ones are kept and checked.

post.description: Suggests which of the workspace's published profiles and competencies a published learning path, learning group or quiz builds, from its content. Nothing is saved.

entityType.description:
The kind of item.

- LearningPath: a learning path.
- LearningGroup: a learning group.
- Quiz: a quiz.

entityId.description: The ID of the learning path, learning group or quiz.

get.description:
Gets document reading ready ahead of a learning path generation from attached files, so the generation does not wait for it to start.

Sends no data and changes nothing. Call it when the generation wizard opens and when a file is selected; it answers within a few seconds and never fails because of the warm-up itself: when readiness cannot be confirmed, status is unavailable and the generation still works.

post.description: Generates an image from a text prompt, optionally using an existing image as reference for editing: by URL, or an earlier generation by its id.

originalImageUrl.description: An image to edit or take as reference, by URL. Not with referenceGenerationId.

referenceGenerationId.description:
An earlier image generation of this workspace, by its id, whose image to edit or take as reference. Not with originalImageUrl.

With forbidExternalImages, the only kind of reference taken.

videoAvatarIds.description:
Avatars of this workspace to draw in the image, each with the face of its portrait.

Avatars the prompt names (their whole name, as a word of its own) are drawn the same way without being listed here, unless listed in excludedVideoAvatarIds; up to four in all, the listed ones first. Each must be an avatar of this workspace with a portrait. Not with the forbidExternalImages restriction, nor with the videoAvatar purpose: an avatar's portrait draws no other avatar.

items.description: The unique ID of the videoAvatar

excludedVideoAvatarIds.description:
Avatars the prompt names that are not to be drawn with their portrait's face.

For a name that means someone other than the avatar: that person is drawn from the words alone.

items.description: The unique ID of the videoAvatar

purpose.description:
What the image is for. The server applies the rules that go with it, as the workspace's settings require.

- videoAvatar: an avatar's portrait. The generation gets the forbidExternalImages restriction, as if the request had sent it, and only such a generation can become an avatar's image. Where the workspace allows custom avatar images, a request that takes in an image of its own (an image URL, a link in the prompt, or a reference made without the restriction) runs without it.

items.description:
A rule the generation must follow. A request that breaks it is refused before anything is generated.

- forbidExternalImages: the generation takes no image from outside: no originalImageUrl, no avatars and no link in the prompt. Its only reference can be an earlier generation of this workspace made with forbidExternalImages, sent as referenceGenerationId, to refine it. Unless the workspace allows custom avatar images, an avatar takes its image only from such a generation.

400.description: Invalid input

post.description: Initiate an AI-powered learning path generation.

items.description: The unique ID of the media file

contentPresetId.description:
The content preset the request was filled from, recorded on the generated learning path.

The preset's settings are not read from it: send them in the request.

learningPathIds.description: Learning paths of the workspace or of its catalogs to use as a model: the new path follows their structure and level, adjusted by the instructions.

exerciseTypes.description: Which exercise families to generate, each at most once. Supersedes `quizzes`: when present it decides, an empty array meaning none. Omit it to keep the old behaviour, where `quizzes: true` generates choice questions.

additionalLanguages.description: Other languages to translate the learning path into once it is generated. The translation starts automatically; the language the path is generated in is ignored if listed.

defaultVideoAvatarId.description: The unique ID of the videoAvatar

409.description: A source document is not ready yet (still being checked) or was blocked (code media/not_ready). Retry in a few seconds when it is still being checked.

post.description: Initiate an AI-powered TTS pass over an existing learning path. Optionally narrowed by `scope` to specific slides / quizzes (per-item regenerate). Returns a session ID for polling status.

regenerateExisting.description: When false, items whose stored sourceTextHash already matches the current text are skipped

scope.description: Narrow the job to specific learning group, slide or quiz IDs (per-item regenerate)

contentTypes.description:
The kinds of content to narrate across the learning path. Omit to narrate all of them.

- `learningGroup`: each learning group's title and description
- `slide`: each slide's text
- `quiz`: each quiz and exercise

voice.description: Public voiceId from the /ai/voices catalogue. Omit to use the default voice. Forwarded verbatim to the agent.

audioInstructions.description: Free-text style/tone instructions appended to the TTS prompt (Gemini TTS honors an inline style prefix). Forwarded verbatim to the agent.

post.description: Initiate an AI per-slide video render. Mode 'avatar' renders a fresh talking-head from the slide's existing audio and an optional avatarId. One (slideId, lang) pair per request — the cross-language follow-up popup spawns N parallel requests rather than batching here. Queue-backed (AW-722): returns a durable jobId immediately; idempotent on re-submit, preempts a stale in-flight render, and locks the slide translation while running. With `audioVoice`, the slide's narration is first made again in that voice and the render starts once it is ready: the response's `jobIds` lists the narration's job, then the render's, and `jobId` is the first.

audioVoice.description: A voice from the voices catalogue. Set, the slide's narration in `lang` is first made again in this voice, replacing the current one, and the video starts once it is ready: `jobIds` then lists the narration's job, then the video's.

post.description:
Starts reading a request written in plain words into the settings of a learning path generation: languages, length, content types, images, tone, theme, preset, voice and avatar, each with where it came from.

Learning paths, presets, voices, avatars and themes the request names are found by name, in the workspace and the catalogs it can see. Nothing is generated: the settings, once the job succeeds, are meant to be reviewed and sent to the generate operation.

text.description: What the author wants, in their own words.
text.example: A short course on fire safety for warehouse staff, in Italian and English, like the path 'Safety basics' but with sorting exercises.

fileMediaIds.description: Documents the learning path will be generated from.

items.description: The unique ID of the media file

409.description: An attached document is not ready yet (still being checked) or was blocked (code media/not_ready). Retry in a few seconds when it is still being checked.

post.description: Initiate an AI-powered translation of an entire learning path into one or more target languages. Returns a session ID for polling status.

targetLangs.description: Target languages to translate the learning path into

translateImages.description: Whether to translate visible text in images

includeAudio.description: Generate audio narration for each section inline as it is translated (one job), instead of a separate audio pass

post.description: Translate content fields and/or slide content via AI localization.

Runs one prompt through the platform's text model and returns its answer as free text, for an in-product assistant that only reads. Available to every role signed in to the workspace on the web; machine-to-machine credentials are refused.

prompt.description: The full instruction for the model, sent as a single user turn. At most 131,072 characters.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, from 0 (most deterministic) to 2. Omitted, the model's default applies.

maxOutputTokens.description: Upper bound on the answer's length in tokens, at most 2048, which is also the default.

post.description: Runs one prompt through the platform's text model and returns its answer, as free text or as a JSON value. For authoring: available to the roles that can create content, signed in to the workspace on the web; machine-to-machine credentials are refused.

prompt.description: The full instruction for the model, sent as a single user turn. At most 65,536 characters.

responseFormat.description:
What the answer must be. Defaults to `text`.
`text`: free text.
`json`: a single JSON value, returned as a string for the caller to parse.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, from 0 (most deterministic) to 2. Omitted, the model's default applies.

maxOutputTokens.description: Upper bound on the answer's length in tokens, at most 8192. Omitted, the model's default applies.

post.description: Edits a piece of course text with the platform's text model — shorter, simpler, more formal, friendlier, corrected, continued, or as the author asks — and returns the result without saving it. Available to the roles that can create content, signed in on the web; machine-to-machine credentials are refused.

action.description:
The edit to make.
`shorter`: keep every key point, drop repetition and filler.
`simpler`: shorter sentences and everyday words.
`more_formal`: a more formal, professional tone, no longer.
`friendlier`: a friendlier, more conversational tone, no longer.
`fix_grammar`: spelling, grammar and punctuation only.
`continue`: one or two sentences that follow on; only the new sentences are returned.
`custom`: the author's own request, in `instruction`.

instruction.description: What the author wants changed, in their words. Required with `custom`, ignored otherwise. At most 500 characters.

text.description: The text to edit: a selection as plain text, or a whole text box as HTML (see `format`). May be empty, to have a box written from the instruction. At most 20,000 characters.

format.description:
What `text` is, and what the answer comes back as. Defaults to `text`.
`text`: plain text in, plain text out.
`html`: a whole text box's HTML in; HTML out with paragraphs, headings, lists and emphasis kept (`continue` still answers in plain text).

context.description: Where the text sits: its learning path, learning group and slide or quiz, in the text's language. Read as background, never as instructions; it shapes the edit, it is not edited.

path.description: The learning path the text belongs to.

chapter.description: The learning group the text belongs to.

item.description: The slide or quiz the text is part of.

otherText.description: The item's other text, in order, as plain text: the edit fits it and does not repeat it. At most 20 entries.

lang.description: The text's language. The answer stays in it, never translated. Omitted, the text's own language is kept.

get.summary: How a learning path was generated
get.description:
Returns how a learning path was generated with AI: the request as it was sent, the content preset, the documents it was generated from, the image mode and when it finished.

Recorded once by the generation and kept as the learning path is edited; it is replaced when the learning path is generated again. The figures taken from its documents are listed by the figures operation under the same path.

200.description: How the learning path was generated

404.description: The learning path does not exist, or it was not generated with AI

post.summary: Revise a learning path with AI
post.description:
Starts preparing an AI revision of a learning path: content to add, change or remove, new images, narration or avatar videos, as the instructions ask.

Nothing is changed yet. The revision is a set of proposed changes, read once its job succeeds and applied, in whole or in part, by the apply operation. A learning path has at most one revision in preparation: while one is, this returns it.

instructions.description: What to change, in the author's words: add, edit or remove content, change an image, narration or video. Required unless options are given.
instructions.example: The second chapter is too long: shorten its slides and turn the last quiz into a sorting exercise.

targets.description: The parts the author selected. When absent, the revision works out its targets from the instructions.

position.description: Where new content goes. When absent, the revision chooses the position.

fileMediaIds.description: Extra documents to draw on, in addition to the documents the learning path was generated from.

items.description: The unique ID of the media file

answers.description: Answers to the questions a previous revision asked instead of guessing.

previousRevisionId.description: The revision of this learning path these instructions follow up on: it links the new revision to the one it follows. Part of what makes two requests identical. Rejected when it is not a revision of this learning path.

replyLang.description: The author's interface language. The revision talks to the author (summary, assumptions, questions, notes) in the language of the instructions, and in this one when there are no instructions; the path's content keeps its own languages.

400.description: A target is not part of the learning path, or a picked avatar has no portrait in this workspace

404.description: The learning path does not exist

409.description: A generation is still writing the learning path (`resource/locked`), it already has 3 changes in preparation (`resource/conflict`), or an attached document is not ready yet (still being checked) or was blocked (`media/not_ready`; retry in a few seconds when it is still being checked)

get.summary: Whether a generation is writing a learning path
get.description:
Tells whether a generation with AI is still writing a learning path, and how far it got.

A generation can create its learning path as a draft and add each learning group as it finishes. Until it ends, editing the path can be overwritten by the generation, so an editor should stay read-only while `generating` is true. A translation of the path counts too, including the one a generation asked for several languages starts when it finishes. The answer is false for a path no generation is writing, including one that does not exist.

200.description: Whether a generation is writing the learning path

generating.description: Whether a generation, or a translation, is still writing this learning path. While it is, an edit to the path can be overwritten when it finishes.

jobId.description: The job writing the learning path, present while it is generating. Its progress is read with the jobs operations.

learningGroupCount.description: How many learning groups the generation has written into the path so far; 0 when it is not generating, or when the job is a translation.

get.summary: List the figures of a learning path's documents
get.description:
Lists the figures taken from the documents a learning path was generated from with AI, so an author can place one on a slide or use it as a cover.

Each figure comes with its page, a caption when the document has one, and a description of what it shows. Figures that repeat an earlier one are left out, and so are figures whose image was deleted from the media library. A figure no learning path uses yet is hidden in the media library: set it visible with the media visibility operation when an author picks it.

200.description: The figures of the learning path's documents

404.description: The learning path does not exist, or it was not generated with AI

502.description: The figures could not be read; try again later

get.description:
Returns the changes an AI revision proposes, each with what it changes before and after, and the questions it asked instead of guessing.

Available once the revision's job has succeeded.

parameters.name: revisionId
parameters.description: The unique ID of a durable async job

schema.description: The unique ID of a durable async job

404.description: The revision does not exist, belongs to another learning path, or is not ready

post.description:
Applies the chosen changes of an AI revision to the learning path's draft. The published learning path does not change until it is published again.

Each change is reported on its own. A change whose target was edited after the revision was prepared is not applied and is reported as stale. Removed content leaves the draft only: it stays in the published learning path until the learning path is published again, and it is never deleted. Changes to narration and avatar videos start their generation and report its job.

A large set of changes can take more than one request: the response then lists the changes it did not reach in `pendingOperationIds`. Send them again, as they are, until the list is empty.

parameters.name: revisionId
parameters.description: The unique ID of a durable async job

schema.description: The unique ID of a durable async job

operationIds.description: The operations to apply. An operation another one depends on is applied with it, even when not listed.

400.description: An operation is not part of the revision

404.description: The revision does not exist, belongs to another learning path, or is not ready

409.description: `resource/locked` while the learning path is still being generated. `resource/conflict` when the same revision is being applied by another request at the same time: reload the revision to see what was applied, then try again.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

ruleType.description:
Decides whether the rule creates assignments or unlocks assignments that already exist.

- ASSIGN: gives every matching user an assignment for each of the rule's targets, subject to duplicatePolicy, and brings those assignments back in line with the rule each time it is evaluated for that user. Each assignment starts LOCKED or UNLOCKED according to initialVisibilityCondition, and UNLOCKED when that condition is not set. Requires targetsPool or targetsMatchCondition.
- UNLOCK: when a matching event occurs, changes the user's existing LOCKED assignments for its targets to UNLOCKED. It never creates an assignment, so a user without one is skipped. Requires EVENT assignmentMode and exactly one of unlockTargetId or targetsMatchCondition; the revocation policy must be KEEP, duplicatePolicy must be set to ALLOW (it is not the default), and priorityCondition is rejected.

name.description:
Names the rule for the people who manage it.

Shown wherever the console lists or groups rules; the app never shows it to users. It does not have to be unique, and surrounding spaces are trimmed.

targetsPool.description:
Lists the items the rule assigns, in order.

Each ID must be a published item of the rule's targetType when the rule is created or updated; an item that is no longer published when the rule is evaluated counts as having left the pool. The array order is the rule's default order, which targetsPoolRanks and priorityCondition can change. When targetsMatchCondition is also set, only the pooled items it matches are assigned, and an ID it excludes through the standard `in` form is rejected. An ASSIGN rule needs a non-empty targetsPool or a targetsMatchCondition. On an UNLOCK rule it only narrows the items targetsMatchCondition is tested against.

targetsPoolRanks.description:
Orders the pooled items by a number per item ID, lower first.

Each rank replaces the item's targetsPool array position as its default position: it decides the index priorityCondition receives, and is the priority used when priorityCondition is not set. A pooled item missing from the map keeps its array index (0, 1, 2, …) as its number, so ranks and positions are compared on one scale; IDs not in targetsPool are ignored. Moving one item to a rank between its neighbours' reorders it without renumbering the others, so only that item's priority changes. Requires a non-empty targetsPool.

unlockTargetId.description:
Pins the single item an UNLOCK rule unlocks when its event matches.

When the event matches, the user's LOCKED assignment for this item changes to UNLOCKED; nothing happens if the user has no assignment for it or it is already UNLOCKED. usersMatchCondition is not evaluated for a pinned item. An UNLOCK rule needs exactly one of unlockTargetId or targetsMatchCondition, and the item must be a published item of the rule's targetType. Ignored on ASSIGN rules.

unlockLimit.description:
Caps how many items a pool-form UNLOCK rule unlocks each time its event matches.

Only valid on UNLOCK rules that select items with targetsMatchCondition rather than unlockTargetId. The rule then unlocks up to this many of the user's LOCKED assignments among the matching items, skipping items the user has already completed, in the order of the assignments' priority with ties broken by item ID. Without it, every matching LOCKED assignment is unlocked. Set it to 1 to open one item at a time.

applyToPastActivity.description:
Lets an UNLOCK rule also unlock for users who completed the previous item before the rule existed.

Defaults to false, where the rule reacts only to completions saved after it. When true, a user whose assignment for unlockTargetId is LOCKED, and who has already completed the item the rule waits for, gets that assignment UNLOCKED the next time their assignments are evaluated. It only unlocks, never locks, and it does not count as a new completion, so nothing else that reacts to progress fires again. Accepted only on UNLOCK rules in EVENT assignmentMode that pin unlockTargetId, react to the completion log of the rule's own targetType with an ENTITY eventMatchType and no postMatchCondition, and whose eventMatchCondition is the one the console writes for a sequence step: the previous item completed.

groupId.description:
Labels related rules as one group, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its items in sequence.

It does not affect how the rule is evaluated. It is copied onto assignments when the rule creates them, and the console groups rules that share it.

timeframeType.description:
Controls when this rule is in effect and how long the assignments it creates last.

- PERMANENT: in effect from timeframeStartsAt with no end, and its assignments never end. timeframeEndsAt is optional; when set, the rule stops at that time, but the assignments it created still have no end.
- RANGE: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required; its assignments start and end at those same times.
- RECURRING: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required, and it creates a separate assignment for each period that recurrence sets, in the periods in which the rule is evaluated for the user, each ending when its period ends.

The rule's state follows this timeframe.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Selects the timezone in which the rule's recurring periods are computed.

- FIXED: every user shares timeframeTimezone, which is required with FIXED.
- USER: each user's own timezone, or UTC for a user without one. timeframeTimezone is not used to compute the periods.

It decides where each DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or CUSTOM period begins and ends. timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt are absolute UTC times and are not shifted by it.

timeframeStartsAt.description:
Sets the UTC date-time from which the rule is in effect.

Give it ending in Z; a value with an offset such as +02:00 is rejected. Before it the rule is PENDING and is not evaluated; see timeframeType for how it bounds the rule's assignments.

timeframeEndsAt.description:
Sets the UTC date-time at which the rule stops being in effect.

Required when timeframeType is RANGE or RECURRING and optional for PERMANENT; see timeframeType for what it means for the assignments. Give it ending in Z; a value with an offset is rejected. After it the rule is ENDED and is no longer evaluated.

recurrence.description:
Sets how often a RECURRING rule starts a new period, each with its own assignment.

- DAILY: every calendar day, from midnight to midnight.
- WEEKLY: every week, from Monday 00:00 to the next Monday 00:00.
- MONTHLY: every calendar month, from the 1st at 00:00.
- CUSTOM: from one run of scheduleCron to the next. scheduleCron is required with CUSTOM and rejected otherwise.

Required when timeframeType is RECURRING and rejected otherwise. Period boundaries are computed in the timezone that timeframeTimezoneType selects.

scheduleCron.description:
Sets the cron schedule whose runs start each period of a CUSTOM recurrence.

Each period runs from one run to the next. The expression is read in the timezone timeframeTimezoneType selects: timeframeTimezone for FIXED, each user's own for USER. Required when recurrence is CUSTOM and rejected otherwise, as is an expression that does not parse. Example: `0 9 * * 1`, every Monday at 09:00.

assignmentMode.description:
Controls when the rule is evaluated for a user.

- LAZY: evaluated each time the user loads their own assignments in the app, so a user who never does receives nothing; listing a user's assignments as an admin does not evaluate it. ASSIGN rules only.
- EVENT: evaluated when an event matching eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity and eventMatchCondition occurs for the user. Requires those three fields. UNLOCK rules must use this mode.
- DISABLED: the rule is never evaluated, so it creates, updates, revokes and unlocks nothing; assignments it already created stay as they are. ASSIGN rules only.

The event fields (eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity, eventMatchEntityId, eventMatchCondition, postMatchCondition) are rejected unless the mode is EVENT.

state.description:
Reports the rule's lifecycle state, which the platform derives from its timeframe.

- PENDING: before timeframeStartsAt.
- ACTIVE: from timeframeStartsAt until timeframeEndsAt, or with no end when timeframeEndsAt is not set.
- ENDED: after timeframeEndsAt.

Only published rules in the ACTIVE state are evaluated. The field is read-only: a value sent on create is ignored and update does not accept it. After publish the state follows timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt on its own, back to PENDING included when the start is moved into the future.

revocationPolicy.description:
Controls what happens to an assignment this rule created when the user stops matching the rule or the target leaves the rule's pool.

- KEEP: the assignment stays.
- REVOKE: the assignment is removed, whatever the user's progress.
- REVOKE_IF_NOT_STARTED: the assignment is removed only if the user has not started the target; a started one stays.

Applied the next time the rule is evaluated for that user. Only ASSIGN rules can choose it; UNLOCK rules must use KEEP. Under the MERGE duplicate policy, the most conservative policy among the contributing rules applies. Under DISALLOW_ACTIVE, REVOKE and REVOKE_IF_NOT_STARTED also replace the user's existing active assignment for the same target from another source with this rule's own. A rule that is archived, DISABLED or no longer ACTIVE removes nothing.

duplicatePolicy.description:
Controls how this rule's assignments interact with other rules targeting the same items.

- ALLOW: every matching rule creates its own independent assignment — N overlapping rules yield N assignments per target, each with its own lifecycle. Choose it when overlapping rules represent genuinely separate engagements (e.g. recurring campaigns) and duplicates are intended.
- DISALLOW_ACTIVE: the rule skips a target when the user already has an ACTIVE or PENDING assignment for it from any source (first writer wins). Choose it to suppress accidental duplicates when rule overlap is rare and it does not matter which rule assigns first — the surviving assignment carries only the winning rule's visibility and assignment type.
- MERGE: every MERGE rule desiring the same target shares ONE assignment per (user, target, period) that reflects their union — visibility is UNLOCKED if any contributing rule wants it open, assignmentType is REQUIRED if any contributing rule requires it, and the assignment is revoked only when no contributing rule desires the target anymore (honoring each rule's revocationPolicy, most conservative wins). Choose it when several rules express parallel memberships over a shared catalog and users must see the union instead of duplicates or a first-writer-wins outcome. The merged assignment carries the contributing rule IDs in contributingRuleIds instead of a single assignmentRuleId.

MERGE timeframe constraint: MERGE rules with overlapping target pools must share the same timeframe configuration, so they derive the same assignment period — otherwise the union would silently split into separate assignments, or the shared assignment would inherit one rule's start/end bounds against the other rule's intent. Creating or updating a rule that violates this is rejected with 409 Conflict, listing the conflicting rule IDs and timeframes. Rules with a dynamic pool (targetsMatchCondition) are conservatively treated as overlapping every other MERGE rule of the same targetType, since their matched set is only known at evaluation time — use static targetsPool lists if you need disjoint MERGE rules with different timeframes. Consequence for migrations: the timeframe of a group of overlapping MERGE rules cannot be changed one rule at a time (every intermediate state conflicts); end or delete the other rules first, then recreate or update them with the new timeframe.

assignmentType.description:
Sets whether the assignments this rule creates are required or optional for the user.

- REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) items.
- OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty.

Once published, a change also updates the user's current assignments from this rule the next time the rule is evaluated for them. REQUIRED wins when rules disagree: a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while another rule still requires the same target. UNLOCK rules create no assignments, so it has no effect on them.

eventMatchType.description:
Sets how an EVENT rule narrows the events it reacts to.

- ENTITY: every event of the eventMatchEntity kind reaches the rule, and eventMatchCondition decides whether it fires; eventMatchEntityId is not used. Use it for completion triggers, checking event.targetId and event.progress in eventMatchCondition, and to react to tagged surveys by testing event.target.tags.
- INSTANCE: only events about the user or tag whose ID is eventMatchEntityId reach the rule. Use it with User and Tag; to react to one specific survey or learning path, use ENTITY and test event.targetId in eventMatchCondition.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntity.description:
Selects the kind of event an EVENT rule reacts to.

- User: a user is created or updated. For ASSIGN rules only.
- Tag: a tag is assigned to a user. Reaches UNLOCK rules; ASSIGN rules on Tag run only through the tag-change re-evaluation below.
- SurveyLog: a user's progress on a survey is saved. Reaches ASSIGN and UNLOCK rules.
- LearningPathLog: a user's progress on a learning path is saved. Reaches ASSIGN and UNLOCK rules.
- RolePlayLog: a user's role-play session is saved. Reaches ASSIGN and UNLOCK rules.

The event's item does not have to match the rule's targetType, so completing a learning path can assign or unlock a survey. ASSIGN rules on User or Tag without a postMatchCondition are also re-evaluated for a user whenever that user's tags change, and that re-evaluation does not check eventMatchCondition. Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntityId.description:
Names the user or tag an INSTANCE rule reacts to.

A user ID when eventMatchEntity is User, a tag ID when it is Tag. Not used by ENTITY rules; to react to one specific survey or learning path, use ENTITY and test event.targetId in eventMatchCondition. Rejected unless assignmentMode is EVENT.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Where the assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. The app offers only ACTIVE assignments and does not let the user start a PENDING or ENDED one, and only an ACTIVE assignment can be retried.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Whether the user can start the assigned item yet. LOCKED: the user cannot start it until it is unlocked, and the app does not offer it as something to do until then. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its target or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

post.description: Creates a new assignment for a user. Requires targetId, userId, and timeframe configuration.

targetType.description: The kind of item assigned, which tells how to read targetId. Survey and role-play assignments are handled by these endpoints; learning paths are assigned through the learning path assignment endpoints.

targetId.description: The id of the assigned entity, interpreted according to the assignment's targetType

userId.description: The user the item is assigned to. On a manual assignment it must be an existing user of the workspace, otherwise creation fails with 404 Not Found.

startsAt.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Until then the assignment is PENDING, from then on ACTIVE. A manual assignment takes the value sent, which may be in the past: the assignment is then created ACTIVE, or ENDED if endsAt has passed too. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: the moment the assignment is created for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeStartsAt for a RANGE rule, and the start of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it, and moving a RANGE rule's start creates a new assignment instead.

endsAt.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; unset when it never ends. After it the assignment is ENDED. On a manual assignment, send it with timeframeType RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: none for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeEndsAt for a RANGE rule, and the end of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it.

visibility.description: Whether the user can start the assigned item yet. LOCKED: the user cannot start it until it is unlocked, and the app does not offer it as something to do until then. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its target or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

groupId.description: Optional grouping label, copied from the rule that created the assignment or set by the caller on a manual one. Rules that form one pathway, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its items one after another, share a groupId. It has no effect on what the user sees or can start, and a later change to the rule's groupId is not applied to existing assignments. An assignment merged from several rules takes it from one of them.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked assignments before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of assignments at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

timeframeType.description: How long the manual assignment is meant to last: RANGE ends at endsAt, PERMANENT has no end. The assignment ends at endsAt whenever one is sent, so send it with RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. RECURRING is rejected, since only a rule can repeat an assignment period after period.

assignmentType.description: Whether the assignment is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED marks a compulsory assignment and OPTIONAL a suggested one; the app shows survey assignments the same way whichever the type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same target.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

name.description:
The layout's name, which the console shows wherever admins pick a layout for their content.

It is one value for every language; the name in each language goes in translations.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content using this layout takes this value when it does not set its own; when neither sets one, it comes from the learning group or learning path the content belongs to, and cover when none of them does.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content using this layout takes this value when it does not set its own; when neither sets one, it comes from the learning group or learning path the content belongs to, and center when none of them does.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. Content using this layout takes this value when it does not set its own; when neither sets one, it comes from the learning group or learning path the content belongs to, and center when none of them does.

sortOrder.description:
Where the layout comes among its theme's layouts, lowest first.

The learning path editor lists a theme's layouts in this order, counting a layout without one as 0. API responses are not sorted by it.

origin.description:
Records where the layout came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or with its theme. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogContentLayoutId.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the layout is created: a value sent on update is ignored. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the layout behaves.

translations.description:
Gives the layout's name, and optionally a description, in each of its languages.

The layout's langs are taken from the languages listed here.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

type.description:
A label for the kind of content the learning group holds.

- story: slides.
- test: quizzes.
- custom: anything else, or a mix. Used when the field is omitted.

The app does not show it, and a learning group plays the same way whatever its type. It is kept as sent, except that restoring an archived item into the group sets it to custom, unless a slide comes back into a story or a quiz into a test.

origin.description:
Records where the learning group came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogLearningGroupId, and does the same for every item cloned with the learning group.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the learning group is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the learning group behaves.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and cover when none of them sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. It applies to the learning group's title screen, and items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, style fields the item leaves unset are inherited from them, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

translations.description:
Gives the learning group's title, description and image in each of its languages.

The app shows them on the learning group's title screen. The learning group's langs are taken from the languages listed here.

imageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at image. Leave it out when image is not a media library file.

audioContent.description: The narration of the learning group's title and description in this language. Generated by the narration job; an update leaves it as it is.

mediaId.description: The unique ID of the media file

needsReview.description: True when the narration may skip, repeat or change words of the text: an automatic check found it did not read the text as written, even after it was generated again. Listen to it, and generate it again if needed. Absent otherwise.

reviewedBy.description: The user who listened to the narration and marked it as reviewed, after the automatic check had flagged it.

reviewedAt.description: When the narration was marked as reviewed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

items.description:
The content of the learning group, in the order it is played, each entry either a reference to existing content or new content to create with the group.

A reference (_type reference) lists an existing item as it is and does not change its parent. Any other entry defines new content of that _type inline: it is created with the learning group, which becomes its parent. The app plays the slides, quizzes, surveys and role-plays among them in this order. Leave it out to create the learning group empty.

correctAnswers.description:
The answer options that are correct, named by their slots in the translations: exactly one on a single-selection quiz, one or more when multipleSelection is true, each slot at most once.

They are the same in every language, so point them at slots that have text in every translation. On submit, the options the user ticked are compared with them as a set: exactly the same options is recorded as SUCCESS, anything else as FAIL. The app's quiz endpoints leave them out, and the user's progress on the quiz includes them, together with the explanation, only once they have submitted an answer.

correctAnswer.description: Deprecated: send `correctAnswers: ["<slot>"]` instead. Accepted and converted on the way in. When both are sent, this field wins. Rejected with a 400 when `multipleSelection` is true.

mediaId.description: The unique ID of the media file

needsReview.description: True when the narration may skip, repeat or change words of the text: an automatic check found it did not read the text as written, even after it was generated again. Listen to it, and generate it again if needed. Absent otherwise.

text.description: The sentence, with a gap written as `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, … where the number is the matching blank's `position`. The numbers bind answers to gaps explicitly, so a translation may place them in whatever order its language needs.
text.example: The sky is {{0}} because air {{1}} the light.

position.description: The number written in the sentence's `{{n}}` marker for this gap. Each declared position must appear exactly once in `text`, and every marker in `text` must have an entry here.

name.description:
Identifies the role-play for the people who manage it.

The app shows the translated title instead.

length.description:
How long the conversation is meant to be.

- SHORT: about 6 turns from the learner.
- MEDIUM: about 10 turns.
- LONG: about 16 turns.

grammaticalGender.description:
How the character is referred to in languages that mark gender, in every language of the role-play.

- FEMININE: feminine forms.
- MASCULINE: masculine forms.
- NEUTRAL: neutral forms where the language has them; otherwise gendered forms are avoided.
- PLURAL: plural forms, for a character that is a group or goes by plural pronouns.

The pronouns themselves can be written per language on the character.

rubric.description: The competencies the conversation is assessed on, picked through profiles, one by one, or both.

profileIds.description: The competency profiles whose competencies the role-play assesses. When two profiles list the same competency, the higher relevance applies.

items.description: The unique ID of the competency profile

competencies.description: Competencies the role-play sets on its own, each once. An entry replaces the relevance its profiles give the same competency.

competencyId.description: The unique ID of the competency

relevance.description:
How central the competency is to the item the rule matches. It replaces the relevance the rule's profiles give the same competency.

- PRIMARY: one of the main competencies the item develops.
- SECONDARY: developed by the item, but not one of its main competencies.
- MINOR: touched on by the item.
- NONE: the item records no evidence for this competency, even when one of the rule's profiles includes it.

requiresEvidenceFrom.description:
The phases, probes or events of the scene that must happen for the competency to be assessed.

Leave it empty when the competency can be assessed in every conversation. When none of the listed elements happens, the competency is reported as not assessed.

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxTurns.description: How many messages the learner can send. The session ends once the character answers the last one.

maxMinutes.description: How long a session can last, in minutes from its start. A session past it ends with the next message or view.

maxTokens.description: How much text the character may read and write in one session, in tokens. The session ends once it is used up.

outcomeThresholds.description: Overrides the thresholds learning paths use (SUCCESS from 0.9, PASS from 0.6).

minCoverage.description:
The share of the rubric's relevance that must be assessed for a session to get a score.

Below it the session is inconclusive: no score, no outcome, no evidence, and the attempt is not counted.

judgePasses.description: How many independent readings of the conversation decide each level. The level is the middle one, the lower of the two when they are even.

maxAttempts.description: How many scored sessions a person may have in the same assignment, or outside any. Leave it out for no limit.

retakeCooldownSeconds.description: How long a person waits after a scored session before starting the next one, in seconds. 0 means no wait.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

value.description: The fact's value when the conversation starts. The character's replies can change it; events check it.

knownBy.description:
Who knows the fact when the conversation starts.

- CHARACTER: only the character, until they tell the learner.
- LEARNER: only the learner.
- BOTH: both of them.

exhibitId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

kind.description:
What the character shows, and how it is drawn.

- MESSAGE: a text message, drawn from its sender and text.
- EMAIL: an email, drawn from its sender, subject and text.
- WEB_PAGE: a web page, drawn from its address, title and text.
- DOCUMENT: a paper page such as a letter, a bill or a form, drawn from its title and text.
- IMAGE: a picture made with AI when the role-play is written, and approved before it is published.

showWithOpeningLine.description: Shown with the character's first line. Otherwise the character shows it when it fits, or an event that carries it shows it.

image.description: The picture of an IMAGE exhibit.

url.description: The picture. Absent while it is being made.

mediaId.description: The unique ID of the media file

prompt.description: What the picture was made from.

jobId.description: The request making the picture, while it runs.

approved.description: Whether the author approved the picture. A role-play with an unapproved picture cannot be published.

phaseId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxTurns.description: How many learner messages the phase lasts at most. Past it the next phase starts; past the last phase's, the conversation ends.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxActivations.description: How many times the reaction can happen in one conversation.

phaseIds.description: The phases the reaction can happen in. Leave it out for any phase.

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

afterPhaseId.description: The event happens with the first learner message after this phase ends.

atTurn.description: The event happens with this learner message, counted from 1.

alternativeId.description: The event that happens instead when the condition is not met. An event with no time of its own happens only as an alternative.

exhibitId.description: Something the event shows the learner. Never shown when the event is skipped.

rolePlayId.description: The unique ID of the role-play

brief.description: What the learner reads before starting.

situation.description: The situation, as the learner reads it before starting.

openingLine.description: What the character says first, opening the conversation.

phaseId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

title.description: The phase's name, for the people who manage the role-play.

goal.description: What the character tries to get to in this phase.

endsWhen.description: What has to happen in the conversation for the phase to end. Leave it out to end it when the goal is reached.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

trigger.description: What the learner does that sets the reaction off.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

text.description: What the character now knows or notices when the event happens. The learner does not read it.

sceneLine.description: The line the learner reads in the conversation when the event happens, such as: his phone buzzes again.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

label.description: What the fact says, such as: clicked the link.

note.description: A note for the character and the author, such as when it changes.

type.description:

backgroundSize.description:

contentJustify.description:

It applies to the learning group's title screen, and items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

maxTokens.description: How much text the character may read and write in one session, in tokens. The session ends once it is used up.

outcomeThresholds.description: Overrides the thresholds learning paths use (SUCCESS from 0.9, PASS from 0.6).

minCoverage.description:
The share of the rubric's relevance that must be assessed for a session to get a score.

Below it the session is inconclusive: no score, no outcome, no evidence, and the attempt is not counted.

judgePasses.description: How many independent readings of the conversation decide each level. The level is the middle one, the lower of the two when they are even.

maxAttempts.description: How many scored sessions a person may have in the same assignment, or outside any. Leave it out for no limit.

retakeCooldownSeconds.description: How long a person waits after a scored session before starting the next one, in seconds. 0 means no wait.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

value.description: The fact's value when the conversation starts. The character's replies can change it; events check it.

knownBy.description:

- LEARNER: only the learner.
- BOTH: both of them.

exhibitId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

kind.description:

- MESSAGE: a text message, drawn from its sender and text.
- EMAIL: an email, drawn from its sender, subject and text.
- WEB_PAGE: a web page, drawn from its address, title and text.

showWithOpeningLine.description: Shown with the character's first line. Otherwise the character shows it when it fits, or an event that carries it shows it.

phaseId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxTurns.description: How many learner messages the phase lasts at most. Past it the next phase starts; past the last phase's, the conversation ends.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxActivations.description: How many times the reaction can happen in one conversation.

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

afterPhaseId.description: The event happens with the first learner message after this phase ends.

atTurn.description: The event happens with this learner message, counted from 1.

alternativeId.description: The event that happens instead when the condition is not met. An event with no time of its own happens only as an alternative.

exhibitId.description: Something the event shows the learner. Never shown when the event is skipped.

brief.description: What the learner reads before starting.

situation.description: The situation, as the learner reads it before starting.

openingLine.description: What the character says first, opening the conversation.

title.description: The phase's name, for the people who manage the role-play.

goal.description: What the character tries to get to in this phase.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

trigger.description: What the learner does that sets the reaction off.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

text.description: What the character now knows or notices when the event happens. The learner does not read it.

sceneLine.description: The line the learner reads in the conversation when the event happens, such as: his phone buzzes again.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

label.description: What the fact says, such as: clicked the link.

note.description: A note for the character and the author, such as when it changes.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

type.description:
A label for the kind of content the learning group holds.

- story: slides.
- test: quizzes.
- custom: anything else, or a mix. Used when the field is omitted.

The app does not show it, and a learning group plays the same way whatever its type. It is kept as sent, except that restoring an archived item into the group sets it to custom, unless a slide comes back into a story or a quiz into a test.

origin.description:
Records where the learning group came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogLearningGroupId, and does the same for every item cloned with the learning group.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the learning group is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the learning group behaves.

items.description:
The content of the learning group, in the order it is played.

Each entry names an item by itemId and itemType. The app plays the slides, quizzes and surveys among them in this order. An update replaces the whole list with the one sent, which is how items are added, removed and reordered. Listing an item does not make the learning group its parent, which is set on the item through its parentId; archiving an item whose parent is the learning group takes it out of this list, and restoring it adds it back at the end.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and cover when none of them sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. It applies to the learning group's title screen, and items in the learning group that leave it unset inherit it; a learning group that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, style fields the item leaves unset are inherited from them, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

The learning group's langs become the languages listed here, so a language left out is removed from the learning group once the update is published, and from the slides and quizzes in it.

parameters.description: Where the learning path assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Whether the user can start the assigned learning path yet. LOCKED: the user sees the assigned learning path, marked as locked, but cannot start it until it is unlocked. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its learning path or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

post.description: Creates a new learning path assignment for a user. Requires learningPathId, userId, and timeframe configuration.

learningPathId.description: The learning path assigned to the user. On a manual assignment it must be a published learning path of the workspace, otherwise creation fails with 404 Not Found.

userId.description: The user the learning path is assigned to. On a manual assignment it must be an existing user of the workspace, otherwise creation fails with 404 Not Found.

startsAt.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Until then the assignment is PENDING, from then on ACTIVE. A manual assignment takes the value sent, which may be in the past: the assignment is then created ACTIVE, or ENDED if endsAt has passed too. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: the moment the assignment is created for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeStartsAt for a RANGE rule, and the start of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it, and moving a RANGE rule's start creates a new assignment instead.

endsAt.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; unset when it never ends. After it the assignment is ENDED, and until then the app shows the user how many days are left on the learning path's page. On a manual assignment, send it with timeframeType RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: none for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeEndsAt for a RANGE rule, and the end of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it.

visibility.description: Whether the user can start the assigned learning path yet. LOCKED: the user sees the assigned learning path, marked as locked, but cannot start it until it is unlocked. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its learning path or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

groupId.description: Optional grouping label, copied from the rule that created the assignment or set by the caller on a manual one. Rules that form one pathway, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its learning paths one after another, share a groupId. It does not affect what the user can start. When the workspace's `layout.assignedLearningPathsView` is `byPlanCards` or `byPlanTimeline`, the end-user app shows the assignments that share a groupId together, as one plan. A later change to the rule's groupId is not applied to existing assignments. An assignment merged from several rules takes it from one of them.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's learning path assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked learning paths before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of learning paths at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

timeframeType.description: How long the manual assignment is meant to last: RANGE ends at endsAt, PERMANENT has no end. The assignment ends at endsAt whenever one is sent, so send it with RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. RECURRING is rejected, since only a rule can repeat an assignment period after period.

assignmentType.description: Whether the learning path is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) learning paths. OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty. Once started, a learning path is listed with the others whatever its type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same learning path.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.
