learningPathRuleId.description: The unique ID of the learning path rule

ruleType.description:
Decides whether the rule creates learning path assignments or unlocks learning path assignments that already exist.

- ASSIGN: gives every matching user an assignment for each of the rule's learning paths, subject to duplicatePolicy, and brings those assignments back in line with the rule each time it is evaluated for that user. Each assignment starts LOCKED or UNLOCKED according to initialVisibilityCondition, and UNLOCKED when that condition is not set. Requires learningPathsPool or learningPathsMatchCondition.
- UNLOCK: when a matching event occurs, changes the user's existing LOCKED assignments for its learning paths to UNLOCKED. It never creates an assignment, so a user without one is skipped. Requires EVENT assignmentMode and exactly one of unlockLearningPathId or learningPathsMatchCondition; the revocation policy must be KEEP, duplicatePolicy must be set to ALLOW (it is not the default), and priorityCondition is rejected.

name.description:
Names the rule for the people who manage it.

Shown wherever the console lists or groups rules; the app never shows it to users. It does not have to be unique, and surrounding spaces are trimmed.

learningPathsPool.description:
Lists the learning paths the rule assigns, in order.

Each ID must be a published learning path when the rule is created or updated; a learning path that is no longer published when the rule is evaluated counts as having left the pool. The array order is the rule's default order, which learningPathsPoolRanks and priorityCondition can change. When learningPathsMatchCondition is also set, only the pooled learning paths it matches are assigned, and an ID it excludes through the standard `in` form is rejected. An ASSIGN rule needs a non-empty learningPathsPool or a learningPathsMatchCondition. On an UNLOCK rule it only narrows the learning paths learningPathsMatchCondition is tested against.

learningPathsPoolRanks.description:
Orders the pooled learning paths by a number per learning path ID, lower first.

Each rank replaces the learning path's learningPathsPool array position as its default position: it decides the index priorityCondition receives, and is the priority used when priorityCondition is not set. A pooled learning path missing from the map keeps its array index (0, 1, 2, …) as its number, so ranks and positions are compared on one scale; IDs not in learningPathsPool are ignored. Moving one learning path to a rank between its neighbours' reorders it without renumbering the others, so only that learning path's priority changes. Requires a non-empty learningPathsPool.

unlockLearningPathId.description:
Pins the single learning path an UNLOCK rule unlocks when its event matches.

When the event matches, the user's LOCKED assignment for this learning path changes to UNLOCKED; nothing happens if the user has no assignment for it or it is already UNLOCKED. usersMatchCondition is not evaluated for a pinned learning path. An UNLOCK rule needs exactly one of unlockLearningPathId or learningPathsMatchCondition, and the learning path must be published. Ignored on ASSIGN rules.

unlockLimit.description:
Caps how many learning paths a pool-form UNLOCK rule unlocks each time its event matches.

Only valid on UNLOCK rules that select learning paths with learningPathsMatchCondition rather than unlockLearningPathId. The rule then unlocks up to this many of the user's LOCKED assignments among the matching learning paths, skipping learning paths the user has already completed, in the order of the assignments' priority with ties broken by learning path ID. Without it, every matching LOCKED assignment is unlocked. Set it to 1 to open one learning path at a time.

applyToPastActivity.description:
Lets an UNLOCK rule also unlock for users who completed the previous learning path before the rule existed.

Defaults to false, where the rule reacts only to completions saved after it. When true, a user whose assignment for unlockLearningPathId is LOCKED, and who has already completed the learning path the rule waits for with the result it requires, gets that assignment UNLOCKED the next time their assignments are evaluated. It only unlocks, never locks, and it does not count as a new completion, so nothing else that reacts to learning path progress fires again. Accepted only on UNLOCK rules in EVENT assignmentMode that pin unlockLearningPathId, react to LearningPathLog with an ENTITY eventMatchType and no postMatchCondition, and whose eventMatchCondition is the one the console writes for a sequence step: the previous learning path completed, optionally with a passed or mastered result.

groupId.description:
Labels related rules as one group, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its learning paths in sequence.

It does not affect how the rule is evaluated. It is copied onto assignments when the rule creates them, and the console groups rules that share it. When the workspace's `layout.assignedLearningPathsView` is `byPlanCards` or `byPlanTimeline`, the end-user app also shows those assignments together, as one plan.

timeframeType.description:
Controls when this rule is in effect and how long the learning path assignments it creates last.

- PERMANENT: in effect from timeframeStartsAt with no end, and its assignments never end. timeframeEndsAt is optional; when set, the rule stops at that time, but the assignments it created still have no end.
- RANGE: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required; its assignments start and end at those same times.
- RECURRING: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required, and it creates a separate assignment for each period that recurrence sets, in the periods in which the rule is evaluated for the user, each ending when its period ends.

The rule's state follows this timeframe.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Selects the timezone in which the rule's recurring periods are computed.

- FIXED: every user shares timeframeTimezone, which is required with FIXED.
- USER: each user's own timezone, or UTC for a user without one. timeframeTimezone is not used to compute the periods.

It decides where each DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or CUSTOM period begins and ends. timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt are absolute UTC times and are not shifted by it.

timeframeStartsAt.description:
Sets the UTC date-time from which the rule is in effect.

Give it ending in Z; a value with an offset such as +02:00 is rejected. Before it the rule is PENDING and is not evaluated; see timeframeType for how it bounds the rule's learning path assignments.

timeframeEndsAt.description:
Sets the UTC date-time at which the rule stops being in effect.

Required when timeframeType is RANGE or RECURRING and optional for PERMANENT; see timeframeType for what it means for the learning path assignments. Give it ending in Z; a value with an offset is rejected. After it the rule is ENDED and is no longer evaluated.

recurrence.description:
Sets how often a RECURRING rule starts a new period, each with its own learning path assignment.

- DAILY: every calendar day, from midnight to midnight.
- WEEKLY: every week, from Monday 00:00 to the next Monday 00:00.
- MONTHLY: every calendar month, from the 1st at 00:00.
- CUSTOM: from one run of scheduleCron to the next. scheduleCron is required with CUSTOM and rejected otherwise.

Required when timeframeType is RECURRING and rejected otherwise. Period boundaries are computed in the timezone that timeframeTimezoneType selects.

scheduleCron.description:
Sets the cron schedule whose runs start each period of a CUSTOM recurrence.

Each period runs from one run to the next. The expression is read in the timezone timeframeTimezoneType selects: timeframeTimezone for FIXED, each user's own for USER. Required when recurrence is CUSTOM and rejected otherwise, as is an expression that does not parse. Example: `0 9 * * 1`, every Monday at 09:00.

assignmentMode.description:
Controls when the rule is evaluated for a user.

- LAZY: evaluated each time the user loads their own learning path assignments in the app, so a user who never does receives nothing; listing a user's assignments as an admin does not evaluate it. ASSIGN rules only.
- EVENT: evaluated when an event matching eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity and eventMatchCondition occurs for the user. Requires those three fields. UNLOCK rules must use this mode.
- DISABLED: the rule is never evaluated, so it creates, updates, revokes and unlocks nothing; assignments it already created stay as they are. ASSIGN rules only.

The event fields (eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity, eventMatchEntityId, eventMatchCondition, postMatchCondition) are rejected unless the mode is EVENT.

state.description:
Reports the rule's lifecycle state, which the platform derives from its timeframe.

- PENDING: before timeframeStartsAt.
- ACTIVE: from timeframeStartsAt until timeframeEndsAt, or with no end when timeframeEndsAt is not set.
- ENDED: after timeframeEndsAt.

Only published rules in the ACTIVE state are evaluated. The field is read-only: a value sent on create is ignored and update does not accept it. After publish the state follows timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt on its own, back to PENDING included when the start is moved into the future.

revocationPolicy.description:
Controls what happens to an assignment this rule created when the user stops matching the rule or the learning path leaves the rule's pool.

- KEEP: the assignment stays.
- REVOKE: the assignment is removed, whatever the user's progress.
- REVOKE_IF_NOT_STARTED: the assignment is removed only if the user has not started the learning path; a started one stays.

Applied the next time the rule is evaluated for that user. Only ASSIGN rules can choose it; UNLOCK rules must use KEEP. Under the MERGE duplicate policy, the most conservative policy among the contributing rules applies. Under DISALLOW_ACTIVE, REVOKE and REVOKE_IF_NOT_STARTED also replace the user's existing active assignment for the same learning path from another source with this rule's own. A rule that is archived, DISABLED or no longer ACTIVE removes nothing.

duplicatePolicy.description:
Controls how this rule's assignments interact with other rules targeting the same learning paths.

- ALLOW: every matching rule creates its own independent assignment — N overlapping rules yield N assignments per learning path, each with its own lifecycle. Choose it when overlapping rules represent genuinely separate engagements (e.g. recurring campaigns) and duplicates are intended.
- DISALLOW_ACTIVE: the rule skips a learning path when the user already has an ACTIVE or PENDING assignment for it from any source (first writer wins). Choose it to suppress accidental duplicates when rule overlap is rare and it does not matter which rule assigns first — the surviving assignment carries only the winning rule's visibility and assignment type.
- MERGE: every MERGE rule desiring the same learning path shares ONE assignment per (user, learning path, period) that reflects their union — visibility is UNLOCKED if any contributing rule wants it open, assignmentType is REQUIRED if any contributing rule requires it, and the assignment is revoked only when no contributing rule desires the learning path anymore (honoring each rule's revocationPolicy, most conservative wins). Choose it when several rules express parallel memberships over a shared catalog (e.g. multi-cohort learning pathways) and users must see the union instead of duplicates or a first-writer-wins outcome. The merged assignment carries the contributing rule IDs in contributingRuleIds instead of a single learningPathRuleId.

MERGE timeframe constraint: MERGE rules with overlapping learning path pools must share the same timeframe configuration, so they derive the same assignment period — otherwise the union would silently split into separate assignments, or the shared assignment would inherit one rule's start/end bounds against the other rule's intent. Creating or updating a rule that violates this is rejected with 409 Conflict, listing the conflicting rule IDs and timeframes. Rules with a dynamic pool (learningPathsMatchCondition) are conservatively treated as overlapping every other MERGE rule, since their matched set is only known at evaluation time — use static learningPathsPool lists if you need disjoint MERGE rules with different timeframes. Consequence for migrations: the timeframe of a group of overlapping MERGE rules cannot be changed one rule at a time (every intermediate state conflicts); end or delete the other rules first, then recreate or update them with the new timeframe.

Sets whether the learning path assignments this rule creates are required or optional for the user.

- REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) items.
- OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty.

Once published, a change also updates the user's current assignments from this rule the next time the rule is evaluated for them. REQUIRED wins when rules disagree: a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while another rule still requires the same learning path. UNLOCK rules create no assignments, so it has no effect on them.

Sets how an EVENT rule narrows the events it reacts to.

- ENTITY: every event of the eventMatchEntity kind reaches the rule, and eventMatchCondition decides whether it fires; eventMatchEntityId is not used. Use it for completion triggers, checking event.learningPathId and event.progress in eventMatchCondition, and to react to tagged learning paths by testing event.learningPath.tags.
- INSTANCE: only events about the user or tag whose ID is eventMatchEntityId reach the rule. Use it with User and Tag; to react to one specific learning path, use ENTITY and test event.learningPathId in eventMatchCondition.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

- User: a user is created or updated. For ASSIGN rules only.
- Tag: a tag is assigned to a user. Reaches UNLOCK rules; ASSIGN rules on Tag run only through the tag-change re-evaluation below.

ASSIGN rules on User or Tag without a postMatchCondition are also re-evaluated for a user whenever that user's tags change, and that re-evaluation does not check eventMatchCondition. Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

origin.description:
Records where the learning path came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogLearningPathId, and does the same for every learning group and item cloned with the learning path.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the learning path is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace is CUSTOM, with no catalogWorkspaceId or catalogLearningPathId. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the learning path behaves; the console's learning path lists can filter by it.

defaultVideoAvatarId.description: The unique ID of the videoAvatar

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Learning groups and items in the learning path that leave it unset inherit it; a learning path that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout, and cover when neither sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Learning groups and items in the learning path that leave it unset inherit it; a learning path that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout, and center when neither sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. Learning groups and items in the learning path that leave it unset inherit it; a learning path that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout, and center when neither sets one.

learningPathId.description: The learning path assigned to the user. On a manual assignment it must be a published learning path of the workspace, otherwise creation fails with 404 Not Found.

userId.description: The user the learning path is assigned to. On a manual assignment it must be an existing user of the workspace, otherwise creation fails with 404 Not Found.

learningPathRuleId.description: The ASSIGN rule that created this assignment (rules with duplicatePolicy ALLOW or DISALLOW_ACTIVE). Unset on MERGE-managed assignments, which carry contributingRuleIds instead.

contributingRuleIds.description: Present on MERGE-managed assignments only: the IDs of the ASSIGN rules (duplicatePolicy MERGE) whose desired state currently contributes to this assignment. The assignment reflects the union of these rules — it is unlocked if any of them wants it unlocked, required if any of them requires it, and revoked only when none of them desires the learning path anymore. Mutually exclusive with learningPathRuleId.

items.description: The unique ID of the learning path rule

groupId.description: Optional grouping label, copied from the rule that created the assignment or set by the caller on a manual one. Rules that form one pathway, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its learning paths one after another, share a groupId. It does not affect what the user can start. When the workspace's `layout.assignedLearningPathsView` is `byPlanCards` or `byPlanTimeline`, the end-user app shows the assignments that share a groupId together, as one plan. A later change to the rule's groupId is not applied to existing assignments. An assignment merged from several rules takes it from one of them.

periodId.description: Identifies the timeframe period and is computed by the platform, never sent by API callers. It is PERMANENT for a permanent timeframe and the start instant in UTC for a date range. For a recurring rule it is the current day (2026-09-24), ISO week (2026-W39) or month (2026-09) in the timezone the rule uses, and for a CUSTOM recurrence the time of the schedule's last run, in UTC.

timeframeType.description: How the assignment's active window is meant to be bounded: RANGE runs from startsAt to endsAt, PERMANENT has no endsAt and never ends. An assignment created by a recurring rule is RANGE and covers one period of the rule, which creates a new assignment for each period.

startsAt.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Until then the assignment is PENDING, from then on ACTIVE. A manual assignment takes the value sent, which may be in the past: the assignment is then created ACTIVE, or ENDED if endsAt has passed too. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: the moment the assignment is created for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeStartsAt for a RANGE rule, and the start of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it, and moving a RANGE rule's start creates a new assignment instead.

endsAt.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; unset when it never ends. After it the assignment is ENDED, and until then the app shows the user how many days are left on the learning path's page. On a manual assignment, send it with timeframeType RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: none for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeEndsAt for a RANGE rule, and the end of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it.

state.description: Where the learning path assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. The app lists only ACTIVE learning path assignments, and only an ACTIVE one can be retried.

visibility.description: Whether the user can start the assigned learning path yet. LOCKED: the user sees the assigned learning path, marked as locked, but cannot start it until it is unlocked. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its learning path or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

assignmentType.description: Whether the learning path is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) learning paths. OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty. Once started, a learning path is listed with the others whatever its type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same learning path.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's learning path assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked learning paths before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of learning paths at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

unlockedAt.description: When the assignment was unlocked, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Set when an UNLOCK rule unlocks it or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED and on one created UNLOCKED.

unlockedByRuleId.description: The UNLOCK rule that unlocked the assignment. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED, on one created UNLOCKED, and when it was unlocked by an ASSIGN rule being evaluated again rather than by an UNLOCK rule.

currentAttempt.description: Which attempt at the learning path the user is on, starting at 1. The user can retry while the assignment is ACTIVE and the current attempt is complete with outcome PASS or FAIL; a retry adds one and starts the next attempt, and a retry in any other situation fails with 409 Conflict. After FAIL the new attempt starts from scratch; after PASS it keeps what the user already did, except quizzes whose outcome was not SUCCESS, which have to be taken again. The progress returned with the assignment is, by default, that of the current attempt.

name.description: Name of the mission configuration. Used only as a human-readable reference

missionType.description: Type of mission (individual or group-based). When set to GROUP, progress is tracked collectively for all users associated with the same tag, according to the mission rules or manual assignment.

matchType.description: Determines how the mission's conditions are matched. When set to INSTANCE, a specific entity ID must be provided in matchEntityId. When set to ENTITY, all instances of the specified entity type are considered. When set to TAG, all entities associated with the specified tag ID are considered.

matchEntity.description: The entity type the mission's conditions apply to. When matchType is set to TAG, matchEntity must be set to Tag.

matchEntityId.description: Specific entity ID for matching, when matchType is INSTANCE or TAG.

matchCondition.description: JSON Logic expression defining the refining conditions that defines if the matched entity contributes to mission progress. Evaluated against: `{ mission }`.
notes: Rule create and update requests reject an expression that cannot be evaluated.
JSON Logic supports a wide variety of operators such as `==`, `and`, `or`, `>`, `<`, etc.
Whether a valid expression matches the intended users or events is not checked.

incrementExpression.description: JSON Logic expression defining how progress is incremented. This will be copied to mission assignments and evaluated at runtime against: `{ mission, user? }`
notes: Rule create and update requests reject an expression that cannot be evaluated.
JSON Logic supports a wide variety of operators such as `==`, `and`, `or`, `>`, `<`, etc.
Whether a valid expression matches the intended users or events is not checked.

targetAmountExpression.description: JSON Logic expression defining the target amount for mission completion. This will be copied to mission assignments and evaluated at runtime against: `{ mission, user? }` (user is optional and only present for INDIVIDUAL missions).
notes: Rule create and update requests reject an expression that cannot be evaluated.
JSON Logic supports a wide variety of operators such as `==`, `and`, `or`, `>`, `<`, etc.
Whether a valid expression matches the intended users or events is not checked.

intermediateLevels.description: Ordered tiers BELOW the final one, whose threshold is targetAmountExpression. Absent means a single-target mission, which is the same thing as a ladder with zero intermediate tiers. timeframeType.description:
Controls when this rule is in effect and how long the missions it assigns last.

- PERMANENT: in effect from timeframeStartsAt with no end, and it assigns its missions once; they start when assigned and never end. timeframeEndsAt is optional; when set, the rule stops at that time, but the missions it assigned still have no end.
- RANGE: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required; it assigns its missions once, and they start and end at those same times.
- RECURRING: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required; it assigns its missions anew in each period that recurrence sets, and each mission ends when its period ends. A missionConfigurationsPool that lists a configuration with intermediateLevels is rejected with 422.

The rule's state follows this timeframe. In each period the rule assigns once per user, or once to the tag of a GROUP rule, on the first evaluation that matches at least one mission configuration; further evaluations in that period assign nothing, even when more configurations match.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Selects the timezone in which the rule's recurring periods are computed.

- FIXED: every user shares timeframeTimezone, which is required with FIXED.
- USER: each user's own timezone, or UTC for a user without one. timeframeTimezone is not used to compute the periods.

It decides where each DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or CUSTOM period begins and ends, and the timezone scheduleCron is read in. timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt are absolute UTC times and are not shifted by it.

recurrence.description:
Sets how often a RECURRING rule starts a new period, each with its own missions.

- DAILY: every calendar day, from midnight to midnight.
- WEEKLY: every week, from Monday 00:00 to the next Monday 00:00.
- MONTHLY: every calendar month, from the 1st at 00:00.
- CUSTOM: from one run of scheduleCron to the next. scheduleCron is required with CUSTOM and rejected otherwise.

Required when timeframeType is RECURRING and rejected otherwise. Period boundaries are computed in the timezone that timeframeTimezoneType selects.

assignmentMode.description:
Controls when the rule is evaluated and assigns missions.

- LAZY: evaluated for a user each time they list their own missions in the app, so a user who never does receives nothing. For INDIVIDUAL rules only: a GROUP rule in LAZY mode is never evaluated.
- EVENT: evaluated when an event matching eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity and eventMatchCondition occurs, for the user the event concerns, or for the tag of a GROUP rule. Requires those three fields and eventMatchEntityId.
- DISABLED: the rule is never evaluated, so it assigns nothing; missions it already assigned stay as they are.

The event fields (eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity, eventMatchEntityId, eventMatchCondition, postMatchCondition) are rejected unless the mode is EVENT.

state.description:
Reports the rule's lifecycle state, which the platform derives from its timeframe.

- PENDING: before timeframeStartsAt.
- ACTIVE: from timeframeStartsAt until timeframeEndsAt, or with no end when timeframeEndsAt is not set.
- ENDED: after timeframeEndsAt.

Only published rules in the ACTIVE state are evaluated. The field is read-only: a value sent on create or update is ignored. After publish the state follows timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt on its own, back to PENDING included when the start is moved into the future.

eventMatchType.description:
Sets how an EVENT rule narrows the events it reacts to.

- ENTITY: every event of the eventMatchEntity kind reaches the rule, and eventMatchCondition decides whether it fires; eventMatchEntityId is still required.
- INSTANCE: only events about the activity, quiz or user whose ID is eventMatchEntityId reach the rule.
- TAG: only activity events recorded with the tag eventMatchEntityId among their tags reach the rule.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntity.description:
Selects the kind of event an EVENT rule reacts to.

- Activity: an activity log is recorded for a user.
- Quiz: a user's answer to a quiz is recorded.
- User: a user is created or updated.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntityId.description:
Names the activity, quiz or user an INSTANCE rule reacts to, or the tag a TAG rule reacts to.

An activity, quiz or user ID for INSTANCE, according to eventMatchEntity, and a tag ID for TAG. ENTITY rules do not use it, but it is required whenever assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise. With eventMatchEntity Quiz it must be the ID of a published quiz, or the create or update is rejected.

actorId.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. userId, principalId, ruleId, or a logical name for system actors.

difficulty.description:
How hard the quiz is meant to be, as set by its author.

It does not affect scoring: an answer is right or wrong whatever the difficulty, and the app does not show it. Each submitted answer records the quiz's difficulty at that moment, so reward, mission and streak rules can test it as event.difficulty, and the console's quiz analytics group results by it.

correctAnswers.description:
The answer options that are correct, named by their slots in the translations: exactly one on a single-selection quiz, one or more when multipleSelection is true, each slot at most once.

They are the same in every language, so point them at slots that have text in every translation. On submit, the options the user ticked are compared with them as a set: exactly the same options is recorded as SUCCESS, anything else as FAIL. The app's quiz endpoints leave them out, and the user's progress on the quiz includes them, together with the explanation, only once they have submitted an answer.

itemIdsInOrder.description: The ids in the order the learner has to reproduce — this order IS the correct answer. Each id may appear once.

items.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

pairs.description: The correct couplings. A right item may be shared by several pairs (many-to-one); a left item appears in exactly one.

leftId.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

rightId.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

origin.description:
Records where the quiz came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogQuizId.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the quiz is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the quiz behaves.

placement.description:
A label for where the quiz is meant to appear.

It is kept and returned as sent.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and cover when none of them sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, style fields the item leaves unset are inherited from them, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

reviewedBy.description: The user who listened to the narration and marked it as reviewed, after the automatic check had flagged it.

reviewedAt.description: When the narration was marked as reviewed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

text.description: The sentence, with a gap written as `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, … where the number is the matching blank's `position`. The numbers bind answers to gaps explicitly, so a translation may place them in whatever order its language needs.
text.example: The sky is {{0}} because air {{1}} the light.

position.description: The number written in the sentence's `{{n}}` marker for this gap. Each declared position must appear exactly once in `text`, and every marker in `text` must have an entry here.

alternatives.description: Other answers accepted for this gap. Gaps whose accepted answers are the same are interchangeable: the learner may fill them in any order, and each accepted answer counts once among them.

text.example: The sky is {{0}} because air {{1}} the light.

position.description: The number written in the sentence's `{{n}}` marker for this gap. Each declared position must appear exactly once in `text`, and every marker in `text` must have an entry here.

alternatives.description: Other answers accepted for this gap. Gaps whose accepted answers are the same are interchangeable: the learner may fill them in any order, and each accepted answer counts once among them.

difficulty.description:
How hard the quiz is meant to be, as set by its author.

It does not affect scoring: an answer is right or wrong whatever the difficulty, and the app does not show it. Each submitted answer records the quiz's difficulty at that moment, so reward, mission and streak rules can test it as event.difficulty, and the console's quiz analytics group results by it.

correctAnswers.description:
The answer options that are correct, named by their slots in the translations: exactly one on a single-selection quiz, one or more when multipleSelection is true, each slot at most once.

They are the same in every language, so point them at slots that have text in every translation. On submit, the options the user ticked are compared with them as a set: exactly the same options is recorded as SUCCESS, anything else as FAIL. The app's quiz endpoints leave them out, and the user's progress on the quiz includes them, together with the explanation, only once they have submitted an answer.

itemIdsInOrder.description: The ids in the order the learner has to reproduce — this order IS the correct answer. Each id may appear once.

items.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

pairs.description: The correct couplings. A right item may be shared by several pairs (many-to-one); a left item appears in exactly one.

leftId.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

rightId.description: Identifier of one item, shared by `itemIdsInOrder` / `pairs` and the keys of `itemLabels`. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters; it may not be a bare number, nor `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

origin.description:
Records where the quiz came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogQuizId.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the quiz is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the quiz behaves.

placement.description:
A label for where the quiz is meant to appear.

It is kept and returned as sent.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and cover when none of them sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, style fields the item leaves unset are inherited from them, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

- SECONDARY: part of the group, but not one of its main competencies.
- MINOR: touched on by the group.

actorId.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. userId, principalId, ruleId, or a logical name for system actors.

name.description:
Names the rule for the people who manage it.

It plays no part in matching an event or granting a reward.

ruleType.description:
Selects what an event must match for this rule to be considered.

- INSTANCE: only events about the one item named by matchEntityId reach matchCondition; only allowed with ALWAYS applicationMode.
- ENTITY: every event of the matchEntity kind reaches matchCondition, which can also test the item's tags.

matchEntity.description:
Names the kind of item this rule matches against.

A rule fires for events about Activity, Quiz, Slide, LearningPath, LearningGroup, Survey, RolePlay, Mission or Streak. A RolePlay event is a scored role-play session, with its outcome, score and attempt.

Required for INSTANCE and TAG rules, together with matchEntityId; for ENTITY rules it alone decides which events reach matchCondition.

matchEntityId.description:
Names the specific item — or, for a TAG rule, the tag — the rule is pinned to.

Required for INSTANCE and TAG rules; ignored for ENTITY rules, which match every item of the matchEntity kind instead.

applicationMode.description:
Controls whether this rule takes part in matching an event.

- ALWAYS: evaluated on every event it could match; every ALWAYS rule that matches fires.
- FALLBACK: evaluated only for an event that no ALWAYS rule in the workspace targets by its entity, item or tag, even when that ALWAYS rule's matchCondition then fails; every matching FALLBACK rule fires.
- DISABLED: skipped — the rule is never evaluated.

INSTANCE rules must use ALWAYS.

rewards.description:
Lists what firing this rule grants, from 1 to 10 entries, each a virtual-currency change, a badge award or competency evidence.

- VIRTUAL_CURRENCY: changes the user's virtualCurrencyId balance by the amount its expression computes from the triggering event, posted with redemptionMode.
- BADGE: awards the user the badgeConfigurationId badge.
- COMPETENCY: records evidence for the competencies of its profiles and its own list. It records evidence only from learning path, learning group and quiz events, so it needs matchEntity LearningPath, LearningGroup, Quiz or Tag, and it is never allowed with FALLBACK applicationMode. The level is SUCCESS 5, PASS 3, FAIL 1 for a learning path or group and 5 for a right quiz answer, 1 for a wrong one, unless its level expression returns another level from 1 to 5; an expression returning null records nothing.

Every VIRTUAL_CURRENCY and BADGE entry is granted independently when the rule fires. COMPETENCY entries count only from the most specific rules carrying one for the item: rules on the item itself, else rules on its tags, else rules on every item of its kind. A most specific rule whose matchCondition fails records nothing, and the less specific ones are not used instead.

badgeConfigurationId.description: Unique identifier for the badge configuration (NanoID).

profileIds.description: The competency profiles whose competencies the rule records evidence for. When two profiles list the same competency, the higher relevance applies.

items.description: The unique ID of the competency profile

competencies.description: Competencies the rule sets on its own, each once. An entry replaces the relevance the profiles give the same competency.

competencyId.description: The unique ID of the competency

relevance.description:
How central the competency is to the item the rule matches. It replaces the relevance the rule's profiles give the same competency.

- PRIMARY: one of the main competencies the item develops.
- SECONDARY: developed by the item, but not one of its main competencies.
- MINOR: touched on by the item.
- NONE: the item records no evidence for this competency, even when one of the rule's profiles includes it.

removeOnPublish.description: Set on a rule pinned to a learning path, learning group or quiz to drop this reward when the item's learning path is next published. Until then the reward keeps recording evidence; saving the rule without it cancels the removal.

currentJudgeSetup.description: The AI judge setup in use: the one that scored the latest role-play or check.

judgeConfigHash.description: Identifies the AI judge's setup (its model and instructions); changes whenever either does.

model.description: The model the AI judge ran on.

promptHash.description: Identifies the version of the AI judge's instructions.

passes.description: How many independent reads the judge gave each conversation.

items.description: Every published competency with where it stands with the AI judge check, provisional ones first.

competencyId.description: The unique ID of the competency

label.description: The competency's label in the caller's language, or in its default language.

status.description:
Where a competency stands with the AI judge check.

- CALIBRATED: its published version passed on the judge setup in use; role-play evidence for it counts in the console.
- PROVISIONAL: it has not passed on that setup; learners still play and score, and the console's competency views leave its role-play evidence out.
- RUNNING: a check is under way.
- NOT_RUN: it was never checked; it is checked when it is published.

reasons.description: Why the competency is provisional; empty otherwise.

items.description:
Why a competency is provisional.

- LOW_AGREEMENT: the judge's levels agree with the written ones less than 0.70.
- BIG_MISSES: the judge gave Advanced to a Basic case, or the reverse.
- UNJUDGED_CASES: too many cases got no usable read.
- OLDER_JUDGE_SETUP: its last check ran on a judge setup that has since changed.
- OLDER_VERSION: its last check ran on an earlier version of the competency.
- RUN_FAILED: its last check stopped before it was scored.

missedLevel.description: The level whose cases the judge most often got wrong in the last check, when it missed any: usually the description to make clearer.

onCurrentSetup.description: Whether the last scored check ran on the judge setup in use now.

runId.description: The unique ID of one run of the AI judge check.

competencyVersion.description: The published version of the competency the run checks.

trigger.description:
What started a run.

- PUBLISH: the competency was published.
- JUDGE_CHANGE: the AI judge's setup changed, or met this competency version for the first time.
- MANUAL: someone asked for it.

status.description:
Where a run stands.

- RUNNING: the test conversations are being written and judged.
- SCORED: every case has the judge's level, and the run has its agreement.
- FAILED: the run stopped before it could be scored; run it again.

judgeSetup.description: The judge setup the run checked; known once it is scored.

judgeConfigHash.description: Identifies the AI judge's setup (its model and instructions); changes whenever either does.

model.description: The model the AI judge ran on.

promptHash.description: Identifies the version of the AI judge's instructions.

passes.description: How many independent reads the judge gave each conversation.

agreement.description: How closely the judge's levels match the levels the cases were written at, from 1 (always) to 0 (no better than chance); the check needs 0.70.

bigMisses.description: Cases written at Basic that the judge gave Advanced, or the other way round; the check needs none.

passed.description: Whether the run passes the check.

progressPercent.description: How far a running check has got, from 0 to 100.

actorId.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. userId, principalId, ruleId, or a logical name for system actors.

rolePlayId.description: The unique ID of the role-play

name.description:
Identifies the role-play for the people who manage it.

The app shows the translated title instead.

length.description:
How long the conversation is meant to be.

- SHORT: about 6 turns from the learner.
- MEDIUM: about 10 turns.
- LONG: about 16 turns.

grammaticalGender.description:
How the character is referred to in languages that mark gender, in every language of the role-play.

- FEMININE: feminine forms.
- MASCULINE: masculine forms.
- NEUTRAL: neutral forms where the language has them; otherwise gendered forms are avoided.
- PLURAL: plural forms, for a character that is a group or goes by plural pronouns.

The pronouns themselves can be written per language on the character.

rubric.description: The competencies the conversation is assessed on, picked through profiles, one by one, or both.

profileIds.description: The competency profiles whose competencies the role-play assesses. When two profiles list the same competency, the higher relevance applies.

items.description: The unique ID of the competency profile

competencies.description: Competencies the role-play sets on its own, each once. An entry replaces the relevance its profiles give the same competency.

competencyId.description: The unique ID of the competency

relevance.description:
How central the competency is to the item the rule matches. It replaces the relevance the rule's profiles give the same competency.

- PRIMARY: one of the main competencies the item develops.
- SECONDARY: developed by the item, but not one of its main competencies.
- MINOR: touched on by the item.
- NONE: the item records no evidence for this competency, even when one of the rule's profiles includes it.

requiresEvidenceFrom.description:
The phases, probes or events of the scene that must happen for the competency to be assessed.

Leave it empty when the competency can be assessed in every conversation. When none of the listed elements happens, the competency is reported as not assessed.

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxTurns.description: How many messages the learner can send. The session ends once the character answers the last one.

maxMinutes.description: How long a session can last, in minutes from its start. A session past it ends with the next message or view.

maxTokens.description: How much text the character may read and write in one session, in tokens. The session ends once it is used up.

outcomeThresholds.description: Overrides the thresholds learning paths use (SUCCESS from 0.9, PASS from 0.6).

minCoverage.description:
The share of the rubric's relevance that must be assessed for a session to get a score.

Below it the session is inconclusive: no score, no outcome, no evidence, and the attempt is not counted.

judgePasses.description: How many independent readings of the conversation decide each level. The level is the middle one, the lower of the two when they are even.

maxAttempts.description: How many scored sessions a person may have in the same assignment, or outside any. Leave it out for no limit.

retakeCooldownSeconds.description: How long a person waits after a scored session before starting the next one, in seconds. 0 means no wait.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

value.description: The fact's value when the conversation starts. The character's replies can change it; events check it.

knownBy.description:
Who knows the fact when the conversation starts.

- CHARACTER: only the character, until they tell the learner.
- LEARNER: only the learner.
- BOTH: both of them.

exhibitId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

kind.description:
What the character shows, and how it is drawn.

- MESSAGE: a text message, drawn from its sender and text.
- EMAIL: an email, drawn from its sender, subject and text.
- WEB_PAGE: a web page, drawn from its address, title and text.
- DOCUMENT: a paper page such as a letter, a bill or a form, drawn from its title and text.
- IMAGE: a picture made with AI when the role-play is written, and approved before it is published.

showWithOpeningLine.description: Shown with the character's first line. Otherwise the character shows it when it fits, or an event that carries it shows it.

image.description: The picture of an IMAGE exhibit.

url.description: The picture. Absent while it is being made.

mediaId.description: The unique ID of the media file

prompt.description: What the picture was made from.

jobId.description: The request making the picture, while it runs.

approved.description: Whether the author approved the picture. A role-play with an unapproved picture cannot be published.

phaseId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxTurns.description: How many learner messages the phase lasts at most. Past it the next phase starts; past the last phase's, the conversation ends.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

maxActivations.description: How many times the reaction can happen in one conversation.

phaseIds.description: The phases the reaction can happen in. Leave it out for any phase.

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

afterPhaseId.description: The event happens with the first learner message after this phase ends.

atTurn.description: The event happens with this learner message, counted from 1.

alternativeId.description: The event that happens instead when the condition is not met. An event with no time of its own happens only as an alternative.

exhibitId.description: Something the event shows the learner. Never shown when the event is skipped.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this role-play belongs to directly. Leave both out for a role-play that stands on its own.

Once the role-play has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the role-play to use it under another parent. The link does not add the role-play to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the role-play puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, publishing them publishes it too, and archiving the role-play takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

resolvedRubric.description: The rubric with its profiles merged and each competency's version, set when the role-play is published. Read-only.

competencyId.description: The unique ID of the competency

relevance.description:
How central a competency is to a group of competencies, such as a profile.

- PRIMARY: one of the main competencies of the group.
- SECONDARY: part of the group, but not one of its main competencies.
- MINOR: touched on by the group.

competencyVersion.description: The published version of the competency, and so of its anchors, the role-play version assesses.

profiles.description: The competency profiles, at the version used, that gave the competency its relevance. Empty when the role-play set it on its own.

competencyProfileId.description: The unique ID of the competency profile

items.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

createdAt.description: Creation date in ISO format (UTC Timezone)

updatedAt.description: Creation date in ISO format (UTC Timezone)

learningPathId.description: The learning path that holds an owned role-play, directly or through its learning groups. Absent for a standalone role-play, and for one whose path could not be read.

actorId.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. userId, principalId, ruleId, or a logical name for system actors.

rolePlayId.description: The unique ID of the role-play

character.description: The character the AI plays. The learner sees only the name; the rest guides how the character behaves.

name.description: The character's name. The brief and the scene write {{name}} where it goes.

pronouns.description: The pronouns the character goes by in this language, as the author writes them, such as she/her, lei or elle. Leave it out to follow the grammatical gender.

who.description: Who the character is: age, job, situation, how they feel walking in.

howTheyTalk.description: How the character talks: tone, pace, the words they use.

wants.description: What the character wants from the conversation.

knows.description: What the character knows and can tell when asked.

doesntKnow.description: What the character does not know, so they never make it up.

hidden.description: What the character keeps from the learner, and when it comes out. The learner never sees it in the brief.

learner.description: The learner's side of the conversation.

role.description: Who the learner plays in the conversation.

canDo.description: What the learner is allowed to offer or decide in the conversation.

aims.description: What the learner tries to achieve, one aim per entry. Shown to the learner and used in the assessment, never to the character.

brief.description: What the learner reads before starting.

situation.description: The situation, as the learner reads it before starting.

openingLine.description: What the character says first, opening the conversation.

phaseId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

title.description: The phase's name, for the people who manage the role-play.

goal.description: What the character tries to get to in this phase.

endsWhen.description: What has to happen in the conversation for the phase to end. Leave it out to end it when the goal is reached.

probeId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

trigger.description: What the learner does that sets the reaction off.

injectId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

text.description: What the character now knows or notices when the event happens. The learner does not read it.

sceneLine.description: The line the learner reads in the conversation when the event happens, such as: his phone buzzes again.

factId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

label.description: What the fact says, such as: clicked the link.

note.description: A note for the character and the author, such as when it changes.

exhibitId.description: The ID of a fact, exhibit, phase, probe or event of the scene, unique within the role-play.

title.description: The exhibit's name, for the people who manage the role-play.

sender.description: Who a message or an email is from.

subject.description: An email's subject, or a web page's or a document's title.

name.description:
Names the leaderboard configuration for the people who manage it.

The console shows it in lists and on the configuration's own pages; the app never shows it, displaying each instance's translated label from translations instead.

displayTopN.description:
Caps how many ranked entries this leaderboard is meant to show, from 1 to 100, defaulting to 10.

It is metadata returned with the rankings for the app to trim its display to; the rankings endpoint's own limit and offset are independent of it and are not capped by this value.

showRank.description:
Whether the leaderboard shows each entrant's position.

When false, the app hides rank numbers throughout, including the viewer's own position, and skips the top-three podium display; when true, both are shown.

showScore.description:
Whether the leaderboard shows each entrant's score.

When false, the app hides the score value everywhere it lists an entry, including the podium; when true, scores are shown alongside ranks.

timeframeType.description:
Sets how long this leaderboard instance stays open and whether the series continues after it closes.

- PERMANENT: the instance never closes and nothing follows it; timeframeEndsAt must not be set.
- RANGE: the instance runs once, from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, both required.
- RECURRING: the instance runs from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, both required, and once it ends a new instance for the next period opens automatically, per recurrence.

Can be changed after creation: switching away from RECURRING drops recurrence, and switching to PERMANENT drops timeframeEndsAt.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Chooses how this instance's active window relates to users in different timezones.

- FIXED: the window runs exactly from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, and timeframeTimezone, which is required, is also the zone RECURRING periods roll over in.
- USER: timeframeTimezone is not used; the instance's state follows timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt as absolute times, and RECURRING periods roll over in UTC.

The scored window itself, timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, is the same absolute time for every user either way.

recurrence.description:
Sets how a RECURRING leaderboard starts its next period once the current one ends.

- DAILY: every calendar day.
- WEEKLY: every week, Monday to Monday.
- MONTHLY: every calendar month.
- CUSTOM: repeats the exact length of the instance's own first period, one period after another, with no calendar alignment.

Boundaries are computed in the timezone timeframeTimezoneType selects, UTC when it is USER. Required when timeframeType is RECURRING and rejected otherwise.

actorId.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. userId, principalId, ruleId, or a logical name for system actors.

origin.description:
Records where the slide came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one. Cloning sets it, together with catalogWorkspaceId and catalogSlideId.
- AI: generated with AI.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the slide is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. It records provenance only and changes nothing about how the slide behaves.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

backgroundSize.description:
How the background image is scaled to the screen behind the content.

- cover: the image covers the whole screen and is cropped where its proportions differ from the screen's.
- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and cover when none of them sets one.

backgroundPosition.description:
Where the background image is anchored on the screen behind the content.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

contentJustify.description:
Where the content sits vertically on its screen: at the top with start, in the middle with center, at the bottom with end.

space-between lays out like start, since the content is a single column. Content taller than the screen starts at the top and scrolls, whatever the value. Content that leaves it unset takes the value from its layout or from the learning group or learning path it belongs to, and center when none of them sets one.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, style fields the item leaves unset are inherited from them, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

sourceFileIndex.description: The position of that document among the files of the generation request, from 0. Set only when source is document.

page.description: The page of the document the figure is on, from 1. Set only when source is document.

rationale.description: Why AI generation chose this image for the slide, in one or two sentences.

figureId.description: The figure's identifier within the documents of the generation, unique across them. Set only when source is document.

figureMediaId.description: The media id of the figure's own image in the media library. Set only when source is document.

description.description: What the image shows, in one or two sentences: the end-user app reads it as the image's accessible text. Set by AI generation when source is document.

mediaId.description: The unique ID of the media file

needsReview.description: True when the narration may skip, repeat or change words of the text: an automatic check found it did not read the text as written, even after it was generated again. Listen to it, and generate it again if needed. Absent otherwise.

reviewedBy.description: The user who listened to the narration and marked it as reviewed, after the automatic check had flagged it.

reviewedAt.description: When the narration was marked as reviewed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

timeframeType.description:
Controls when this rule is in effect and how long it runs.

- PERMANENT: in effect from timeframeStartsAt, with no end required — timeframeEndsAt can still be set to stop it at a given time.
- RANGE: in effect from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, which is required.

Once timeframeEndsAt passes, the rule stops being evaluated and its users' active streaks are marked ended.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Selects the timezone used to compute this rule's daily and weekly periods.

- FIXED: every user shares timeframeTimezone, which is required with FIXED.
- USER: each user's own timezone, or UTC for a user without one.

It decides where a DAY or WEEK period begins and ends. timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt are absolute UTC times and are not shifted by it.

cadence.description:
Sets how often the user must act to keep the streak alive.

- DAY: the user must contribute a matching event every calendar day.
- WEEK: the user must contribute at least once every ISO calendar week.

Missing a required day or week breaks the streak, unless freezeEnabled lets the user spend virtual currency to keep it going. DAY cadence only accepts DAYS as the metric.

metric.description:
Sets what each increment of the streak's counters represents.

- DAYS: one active day.
- WEEKS: one active week.

Must be DAYS when cadence is DAY, which create checks. Fixed when the rule is created; update cannot change it.

freezeEnabled.description:
Lets the platform spend virtual currency on the user's behalf to preserve the streak instead of breaking it when a required period is missed.

Requires freezeVirtualCurrencyId. The balance check and deduction happen automatically when a period is missed, with nothing for the user to confirm. When disabled, or when the balance is not enough, a missed period breaks the streak instead.

goalTargets.description:
Lists up to 10 milestone counts the user can reach within a single streak run.

Each target is tracked and completed independently as the count reaches it, and reaching one notifies the user without affecting the others. Once the highest target in the list is reached, tracking restarts from zero for a new cycle toward the same targets. Order in the list does not matter. Leave unset to track the streak's length without milestones.

title.description:
The survey's name, shown to users as the title of their survey assignments and to admins across the console.

It is one value for every language, not a translation. Survey search matches it as full text and can sort by it.

origin.description:
Records where the survey came from.

- CATALOG: copied from a catalog workspace, on its own or inside a learning path or learning group cloned from one.
- CUSTOM: created in this workspace. Used when the field is omitted on create.

It is fixed when the survey is created: a value sent on update is ignored, and a copy cloned within the same workspace keeps the source's value. Survey search can filter on it; beyond that it records provenance only and changes nothing about how the survey behaves.

backgroundImageMediaId.description: The id of the media library file at backgroundImage. Leave it out when backgroundImage is not a media library file.

parentType.description:
Whether parentId names a learning group or a learning path, the parent this item belongs to directly.

Once the item has a parent it cannot move to another: an update that names a different parentId or parentType is rejected with 409 Conflict, so clone the item to use it under another parent. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. Through it, editing the item puts the learning group and learning path above it back into draft until they are published again, and archiving the item takes it out of the parent's items, while restoring it adds it back at the end.

tagRuleType.description:
Sets whether the rule's tagsPool is meant to be added to matching users or removed from them.

- ADD: tagsPool would be added to users who match usersMatchCondition.
- REMOVE: tagsPool would be removed from users who match usersMatchCondition.

tagsPool.description:
Lists the tags this rule's tagRuleType would add to or remove from matching users, at least one required.

Each ID must reference a published tag, checked when the rule is created and when it is updated.

items.description: Unique identifier for the tag

assignmentMode.description:
Selects which trigger the rule is configured for: on read (LAZY), on a matching event (EVENT), on a schedule (SCHEDULED_PUSH), or never (DISABLED).

- EVENT: requires eventMatchType, eventMatchEntity and eventMatchCondition, all of which are rejected for every other mode.
- SCHEDULED_PUSH: rejected on create and update.

eventMatchType.description:
Selects how the rule would narrow the events matched by eventMatchEntity: by one specific entity or tag id, or by every event of that kind.

- INSTANCE: only events about the single entity identified by eventMatchEntityId.
- ENTITY: every event of the eventMatchEntity kind, without pinning an id.
- TAG: only events about the single tag identified by eventMatchEntityId.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntity.description:
Selects which kind of entity or tag eventMatchEntityId identifies, or which kind of event ENTITY-type matching reacts to.

Required when assignmentMode is EVENT and rejected otherwise.

eventMatchEntityId.description:
Identifies the single entity or tag eventMatchType narrows to when it is INSTANCE or TAG — the value of that item's own id.

Not used when eventMatchType is ENTITY. Rejected unless assignmentMode is EVENT.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the person, for matching them with your systems; GET /users/by-external-id/{externalId} finds the user by it. Creating a user with an externalId that another user of the workspace already has is rejected with 409 Conflict.

nickname.description: The name the person goes by in the app, shown there in place of their first and last name. It must be unique within the workspace: a nickname another user already has is rejected with 409 Conflict. The app asks a person who has none to choose one when they sign in, and notification emails greet the person by it.

currency.description: The person's own choice of currency for money amounts, as an ISO 4217 code; unset when they have not made one.

role.description:
The person's role in the workspace, which decides what they may do and which apps they can sign in to.

- owner: everything an admin can do, and the only role that can give or remove the owner role, since a role can be assigned only at or below the assigner's own.
- admin: creates, edits, publishes and deletes content, manages users and changes the workspace settings.
- manager: creates, edits and publishes content, but cannot delete it, manage users, change the workspace settings or read analytics in the console.
- member: reads content and submits answers in the app, and cannot sign in to the console.
- viewer: reads everything, the console included, but submits nothing and changes only their own profile.

A caller can give only a role at or below their own, and only an admin or an owner can give viewer; machine credentials act as admin, so they cannot create an owner. Any other role is rejected with 403.

status.description:
Whether the person can use the workspace.

- active: the person can sign in, and takes one of the workspace's seats.
- suspended: the person cannot sign in and is told to contact their administrator; the app signs them out if it is open, and any other session ends when it next refreshes. Their record and history are kept, and their seat is given back.

Only admins and owners can change it. Reactivating a suspended user takes a seat again, and fails when the workspace has none free.

referredCount.description: How many people have joined the workspace through this user's referral. It starts at 0 and the platform adds one each time someone joins with the user's referral code or referral link; rule conditions on users can test it.

sub.description: Identifies the principal's sign-in account. The platform assigns it when the principal is created and it never changes; callers never send it.

emailDeliverabilityStatus.description:
The platform's verdict on whether email can reach the principal's address.

- OK: email is sent as usual.
- BLOCKED_MALFORMED: the address is not well formed, so no email is sent to it.
- BLOCKED_NO_DNS: the address's domain cannot receive mail, so no email is sent to it. An address whose domain ends in .test, .example, .invalid or .local always gets this status, without a check.
- BLOCKED_DISPOSABLE: the address belongs to a temporary-mail provider. Email is still sent, but the address cannot start a self-service trial.
- BLOCKED_RANDOM: the address looks randomly typed. Email is still sent, and a self-service trial is refused only when the mailbox cannot be found either.

No email means none at all: sign-in codes, invitations, welcome emails and notifications are all withheld, so the person cannot sign in with an emailed code. Neither the app nor the console shows this status. The platform sets it once, when the principal is created or, if it is unset, the next time the person is sent a sign-in code; callers never send it. While it is unset email is sent as usual, and a check that cannot be completed gives OK.

firstName.description: The person's first name, shared by every workspace they belong to. It is set when the principal is created, from the person's sign-up, their invitation or the admin who created their user, and no invitation or user creation that follows for the same email address changes it. The console shows it with lastName to identify the person; the app shows the nickname instead when there is one.

lastName.description: The person's last name, shared by every workspace they belong to. It is set with firstName when the principal is created, and no invitation or user creation that follows for the same email address changes it.
